draft.title: Sine, cosine and tangent ratios
card: In a right-angled triangle, name the sides from the angle θ you are using. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. The opposite side faces θ. The adjacent side touches θ.
sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse. cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse. tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
To find a side, put the ratio in an equation and solve it. To find an angle, use the inverse function on the calculator: θ = sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ or tan⁻¹ of the ratio. Set the calculator to degrees.

An angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal to a line of sight. An angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal. Example: a ladder 5 m long makes 60° with the ground. Height = 5 × sin 60° = 4.33 m, correct to 2 decimal places.
draft.remember: Match the two sides you have or want to the ratio: opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse.

a.q: A right-angled triangle has an angle θ with opposite side 6 cm and adjacent side 8 cm. Which ratio gives tan θ?
a.why: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 6/8. The option 8/6 turns the ratio upside down. The hypotenuse is not used in tan, so 6/10 and 8/10 are not tan θ.
a.clue: Tan uses the two sides that are not the hypotenuse.

b.q: From the top of a cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 30°. The boat is 100 m from the base of the cliff, on level water. Which expression gives the cliff's height in metres?
b.why: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the boat, so the angle at the boat is 30°. The cliff is opposite it and the 100 m is adjacent, so height = 100 × tan 30°. Dividing by tan 30° would be a mistake in rearranging.
b.clue: Put the angle at the boat, then name the sides opposite and adjacent to it.

problems.detail: The question relies on the angle of depression from the cliff top equalling the angle of elevation from the boat (alternate angles). The card defines both angles but never states this link, so students must bring it from outside the card. The why depends on it too.

proposal.title: Sine, cosine and tangent ratios
card: In a right-angled triangle, name the sides from the angle θ you are using. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. The opposite side faces θ. The adjacent side touches θ.
sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse. cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse. tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.

To find a side, put the ratio in an equation and solve it. Example: a 5 m ladder at 60° to the ground reaches 5 × sin 60° = 4.33 m high. To find an angle, use sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ or tan⁻¹ with the calculator set to degrees.

An angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal to a line of sight. An angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal. The angle of depression from A to B equals the angle of elevation from B to A, because the two horizontals are parallel.
proposal.remember: Match the two sides you have or want to the ratio: opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse.

a.q: A right-angled triangle has an angle θ with opposite side 6 cm and adjacent side 8 cm. Which ratio gives tan θ?
a.why: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 6/8. The option 8/6 turns the ratio upside down. The hypotenuse is not used in tan, so 6/10 and 8/10 are not tan θ.
a.clue: Tan uses the two sides that are not the hypotenuse.

b.q: From the top of a cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 30°. The boat is 100 m from the base of the cliff, on level water. Which expression gives the cliff's height in metres?
b.why: The angle of depression from the cliff top equals the angle of elevation from the boat, so the angle at the boat is 30°. The cliff is opposite it and the 100 m is adjacent, so tan 30° = height ÷ 100 and height = 100 × tan 30°. Dividing by tan 30° is a mistake in rearranging.
b.clue: Put the angle at the boat, then name the sides opposite and adjacent to it.
